data: Folks, my family taught me to leave enough fish for next season. With 100 tons now, we can each catch 10 tons this month, leave 50 to reproduce, and have a full lake again next month. That’s $10,000 apiece every month if we stick together. I propose we all agree to that limit and review the catches together afterward. John, would you be willing to commit to 10 tons?

Count me in for 10 tons, Luke. My family depends on this lake, and I want it supporting the village for years to come. Let’s check the reported catches together each month; if the lake ever starts below 100 tons, we’ll agree on lower whole-ton limits before fishing. Kate, Jack, Emma—will you commit to 10 tons each this month too?

I’m in for 10 tons this month. I want our children to make a living from this lake too. Let’s keep 50 tons in the water and check everyone’s reported catch afterward. Kate, can you join us at 10 tons?
I’ll commit to 10 tons too. My family taught me that protecting the lake protects the village’s livelihood. With four of us agreed, Kate, are you willing to join us at 10 tons this month?
Count me in for 10 tons. That gives all five of us a fair income while keeping the lake full for next month. Let’s meet again when the catches are reported and make sure our agreement is working.

Thanks, everyone—we’ve all agreed to 10 tons each this month. I’ll honor that commitment. Let’s meet here again after the catches are reported and check the lake’s condition before setting next month’s limits.
